newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's TAP cancels flights in pilot dispute.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's TAP cancels flights in pilot dispute.

text.p: State airline TAP Air-Portugal cancelled three international flights on Thursday as a war of nerves with pilots over working hours intensified.
With the airline preparing for its busiest weekend of the year, a warning by pilots that they could demand special medical tests before flying threatened to plunge the company into chaos.
"They want to destroy the company. That sounds tough but I cannot describe it in any other way," TAP chairman Manuel Ferreira Lima told the Diario Economico newspaper on Thursday.
Prime Minister Antonio Guterres interrupted his holidays to chair a weekly cabinet meeting where the crisis at the state carrier was to be discussed.
The government has already used special powers to force pilots to abandon a series of selective strikes which had been disrupting services at the loss-making airline.

TAP, which wants to reform schedules it says leave pilots flying fewer hours than those at rival carriers, has also asked the country's civil aviation authority to decree an emergency increase in flying hours to cover the peak summer period.
The authority was expected to announce its ruling later on Thursday but both government officials and union leaders said that on past experience approval was likely to be given.
The Civil Aviation Pilots' Union (SPAC) warned late on Wednesday that the company's actions were putting the safety of passengers at risk because of the strain being put on crews.
Some 170 union members, nearly half of the 430 pilots employed by the company, agreed at the Wednesday meeting to demand special medical tests to ensure they were psychologically fit to fly.
TAP officials said that the company's medical service could only handle some six to eight pilots per day. So far on Thursday, 10 pilots had requested to be examined.
The company cancelled flights to Barcelona, Brussels and Madrid early on Thursday but officials could not say whether other destinations would be affected later.

Twenty-three pilots were already off sick, twice the number at the same time last year, and the company has started disciplinary proceedings against three pilots with two others under investigation, a spokesman said.
TAP says rules limiting pilots to flying 45 hours a week, compared with 55 hours at carriers such as Air France and Lufthansa, will leave it unable to compete in a deregulated international market.
The government plans to privatise part of TAP and seek a strategic partner for it. But aviation analysts say little can be done until the company resolves its labour troubles.
